text: My kid has been coming here for Occupational Therapy class. The staff are highly qualified and very friendly. The Prompt center on the second floor also offers Thai massage (350 baht for 90 min) and physical therapy. They are quite popular so making a reservation in advance is recommended. The building is new and there are plenty of parking.

The **Chiang Mai University Health Center** is an excellent facility that provides top-notch healthcare services to students, staff, and the public. Located conveniently within the university, the center is easy to access for those in need of medical care. The center is well-equipped with modern medical tools and staffed by friendly and professional healthcare providers who are always ready to assist. It offers a range of services, including general consultations, health check-ups, and preventive care. The atmosphere inside is calm and welcoming, helping patients feel at ease. Whether you're looking for treatment for a minor illness or a routine health check, the Health Center is a reliable place that ensures your well-being. It’s a great resource for the university community and offers affordable care to support a healthy lifestyle.
As an intentional student, we got worst experience from CMU health center. Worse than you can imagine.

The bald guy who takes care of the queue speaks to customers with a condescending tone. Not worth visiting if you need urgent medical attention or seek a health certificate. After you've seen the doc, there won't be anyone telling you where to go to next. Worst service ever. Wondering if they've ever checked all these negative reviews people have left. The bespectacled cashier seems to be the only one who knows what it means to have service mind.

For international students studying in CMU, I do not recommend to go to the CMU health Centre for minor health problems. The customer service is really bad and most of the staffs are really impatient and unhelpful, especially the ones from the queue counter and the pharmacy counter . Specifically, the one who seems bald, he might treat you so bad by pointing his finger according to you are a foreigner. Besides, it takes so long to see the doctor and you need to spend half of your time in a day by waiting the queue to consult with the doctor. Anyway, doctors can communicate in English very well. Despite the fact that the experience is not satisfied, there is one staff at Station 1, who is willing to help to the patient for any causes. Please directly go to see him for next processes.
Very slow service and unprofessional staff. If you need help go somewhere else. Minimum 2 hour wait for just a check up. Worst experience ever :(
The service is excellent. The nurses are lovely. The place is clean. There's a short wait, but not too long. I've used their services several times and I'm always impressed. 😊❤️ …

Clean, spacious, comfortable seating. Parking is available nearby as it's located within CMU (Chiang Mai University).

Monday-Friday 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM
Saturday 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM
Closed Sundays.

Excellent operating hours. Offers comprehensive services: wound care, various vaccinations, reasonable prices, check-ups, general medical care. Good service from nurses, doctors, and staff. Many students use the service.

Cons: Very few staff members, very slow service. The system seems inefficient; numbers disappear, causing delays and queue movement. Signage is unclear, making it confusing on your first visit. However, the staff are very helpful, guiding you and pointing out the correct direction.

Clearer signage and directions would greatly improve service time and assist the staff. The staff are all lovely.

If you're reading this review, I recommend going somewhere else...
Let me vent like a friend.

I went to Suan Dok Hospital, but the nurse there told me to go to Phai Lom instead. So I came. I'd heard beforehand that the service there was bad, from both professors and students.

Let me tell you, the nurses here are lovely. They're polite, patient, and helpful.

The older male doctor I saw was the problem. At first, we were talking nicely, but later he became very angry and yelled loudly. I have problems with frequent bowel movements and severe abdominal pain before defecating. The doctor said, "Everyone poops, everyone has abdominal pain before pooping." He emphasized the word "poop" very strongly. I tried to be polite by saying "pooping," and I tried to explain how much pain I was experiencing, but he kept interrupting me before I could finish. I'm not a good speaker, so I wrote down what I wanted to say on my phone, but I barely spoke because he kept cutting me off. He told me to take care of myself, about my eating and sleeping habits. He asked what faculty I was studying in. I said business administration. He then said, "You can't even manage a business yet." I never expected that to come out of a doctor's mouth. We understand that they couldn't prescribe medication because diarrhea is common and usually resolves on its own without medical attention. However, we needed a medical certificate because it was causing us to be late for our exam. When we explained this, the doctor said they would only issue a certificate stating "frequent bowel movements." We were surprised that our explanation of severe abdominal pain before the bowel movements didn't matter at all – we were in so much pain we could barely walk! The doctor even shook their head in exasperation while entering information into the computer. But the actual certificate stated, "Reported abdominal pain causing late exam." It was clear they intended it to sound bad. We overheard the nurses exchanging glances when printing the certificate; they probably understood the doctor's reasoning. We were shocked that strangers could speak to each other like that.

We gritted our teeth the whole time we got there. Our ears were ringing, and we were on the verge of tears. We were already afraid of talking to strangers, and today's fear intensified. We probably won't dare talk to a doctor again for a long time. 😂

I previously visited the Pailom Clinic at Chiang Mai University (CMU) due to blurred vision and fainting spells. However, I felt I wasn't thoroughly examined and was advised to go home. About three months later, my symptoms worsened to the point of severe blurred vision, so I decided to seek treatment at Suan Dok Hospital. There, they discovered a hole in my retina requiring surgery.

I am very upset and disappointed. If a more thorough examination had been conducted initially, the problem might have been detected earlier and could have been treated with laser instead of surgery. I urge the clinic to improve its patient care and conduct more thorough examinations to prevent other patients from experiencing the same issue.

On the first floor, we saw lovely and kind doctors. They even asked if we needed a medical certificate. The nurses were also very kind, asking if we needed one. Since I was sick and had a dental appointment, the nurse suggested I do the dental work first and then come back down (I had my teeth cleaned and fluoride applied, which didn't take long). I arrived just in time for my turn. The second time I went, the nurses explained everything clearly. At point number 9, they were very kind, telling me to wait and asking if I needed a medical certificate. No one was rude or dismissive. I didn't have to wait long at all. I can't give separate ratings, so I'm giving it 5 stars! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
The Thai massage service was excellent, perfect for students like me who suffer from back, neck, shoulder, and back pain from studying MT (medical science) and a lot of bending and sitting. 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
I'd like to commend the dentists; they were very polite. However, during the teeth cleaning, water splashed all over the cloth. And when they applied fluoride, they used the wet side to cover my eyes again. Please improve this. When wiping with water, please be mindful of the person's nostrils. They covered my nostrils so tightly that I couldn't breathe and couldn't raise my hand because the doctor said it would be too much. I tried to explain by crying and raising my hand, but they still wouldn't listen. Next time I have an appointment, I'll remind them beforehand. 🌟

At first, I was hesitant to come here after reading the reviews.
When I arrived at the door and saw the sign saying there was only one doctor available today, I was a bit discouraged. But once I got there myself, the entire process took about an hour and 40 minutes.

I was very impressed.
It wasn't crowded, and the queue numbering system was clear.

#CMUHealthCenter, a beautiful new building with stylish brickwork. 🧱 Complete with a full range of services, including doctors, physical therapy, child development, dentistry, a pharmacy, and an eyeglasses shop.

There's also a food court with a variety of delicious dishes and plenty of seating to enjoy the cool breeze.
Steak, curry rice, som tam, crispy pork rice, noodles, shaved ice, and drinks.
#ArinsAroyAround
I was very impressed with the service. The staff were attentive, the service process was clear, and the area was spacious and clean. It's a health center of comparable quality to a large hospital.
The service was fast, and the doctors, nurses, and staff were very efficient.

The doctor was very confused. Everyone wants to get better, and I understand that staying up late is bad for your health, but there was a reason I had to stay up late, and he just kept scolding me. I was so confused; I was sick and then I encountered an old male doctor who was radiating negative energy. I recommend going to Suan Dok Hospital instead.

text: I brought my boyfriend to get vaccinated. It was a weekday afternoon, not many people, but the management was terrible! We waited for 3 hours. The price is cheap, but I wouldn't recommend going there.

The service was terrible. The stated opening hours are 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, but I arrived at 2:10 PM and the nurse at the reception desk said they weren't accepting patients that day and told me to come back the next day, even though the hours are clearly displayed (8:00 AM - 4:00 PM).

Came for an X-ray at 3:00 PM. The clinic informed me that I would have to wait for the examination at 4:30 PM. At 5:30 PM, the doctor still hadn't arrived. It wasn't like I had to wait long for the examination. And there were a lot of patients. It's understandable that there were a lot of patients, but the doctor didn't come on time. Previously, I've used the service and it was very fast and convenient. I'd like to see a little more information about where the problem was or why it was late.

The place is new and very clean. I came on a Monday evening and there weren't many people, but I had to wait quite a while for the examination. The nurses were lovely and the doctor gave excellent advice. He examined me thoroughly, so I might have to wait a bit longer.

The nursing staff are very kind, the place is clean, and the queues aren't long for those getting wound care or minor illnesses. However, walk-in patients often have to wait a long time to see a doctor. The location is very convenient, like a clinic but with access to skilled doctors and professional nurses. There's parking across the street. I recommend their wound cleaning service; it's convenient and clean, but it's best to make an appointment beforehand.

This is a very large clinic for students and those affiliated with Chiang Mai University (CMU) who have health issues. It is quite crowded in the late afternoon and early evening. Vaccination services are available and seem to be the …
It might depend on the doctor's schedule, but the other staff members provide excellent service. Personally, the doctors I've encountered have been very helpful and efficient.
The payment counter called me to wait in line to pay. I stood there for a long time, but there were no staff members inside.
I got my vaccine here. The price was good and the service was quick. The doctors and nurses gave excellent advice.

On April 28th at 10:00 AM,
I went for a Thai massage
here for the first time. The counter staff were welcoming.
The male massage therapist was polite and friendly, so I started a conversation with him
to get to know him better and hopefully use his services again in the future.
While he was massaging my left leg (the first step),
a female staff member parted the curtain to look in,
and then left. A moment later, the same female staff member parted the curtain again
and told me to lower my voice.
I immediately stopped talking to the male massage therapist and didn't speak to him again until the massage was over.
I then got dressed and left.
I would like to criticize this female staff member.
You lacked maturity
and the manners expected of a service provider.
You should study and find a better way
to guide clients,
instead of directly requesting them to speak louder. This made me, as a client, feel disgusted and unwilling to use your services again.
I want to emphasize that
I spoke with the male massage therapist in a normal tone of voice; it wasn't a celebratory conversation, and it was a casual discussion.
The first time, during a massage that lasted less than
ten minutes, I, a retired civil servant and former military officer, know
social etiquette and what is appropriate and inappropriate. Therefore, I requested that the head of this department
train the staff on manners, kindness, and leniency
in general, especially
first-time customers like myself.
Luckily, I'm not a hot-headed person.
I might have retorted, "What's with all this fuss? I paid 250 baht for this service. Don't be so pretentious," or even gotten up and stormed out.
That's not the behavior of a gentleman.
I don't accept an apology, but I ask that this staff member improve their behavior.
While it wasn't a serious offense,
they should respect and be accommodating
to customers. Even if they claim I disturbed others, I still
swear I spoke in a normal tone of voice
and the conversation wasn't long. Anyone who heard it,
please don't be so pretentious.
I also paid for this service.
Same as you all.
Suggestion: A large notice should be posted:
No talking or shouting while getting a massage. Anyone who reads it will understand and strictly adhere to the rules.
Thank you. Signed, Colonel Chatukorn Rattanagos, Patient at the Health Center, Chiang Mai University.

text:
It's better to go somewhere else. It's worth spending a little more for your mental well-being. I went to see a doctor here, and he asked, "Why did you come? You didn't need to come for this."

I came to see a doctor, and I waited for hours because my symptoms were unusual. Normally, when I'm sick, I don't go to the doctor; I just take regular medicine and I'm fine because I'm generally not prone to illness. But this time, my body was acting strangely, so I came to find out what was wrong. Being sick every day like this is agonizing, and I just want to get better. When the doctor said that, I walked out of the clinic crying. It was so emotional and infuriating.

text:
I traveled from a district outside the city to seek medical treatment. I checked online and found that Pai Lom was open during the hours listed on their website, so I arrived there after finishing my studies.
I arrived at Pai Lom at 2:40 PM with three days of earache and sore throat on one side of my body. I had no fever or anything. Normally, during this COVID-19 surveillance period, I'd be separated to a room outside the building for testing. I understood, but when I met the nurse, she told me that the testing schedule was over because today was a public holiday, Pai Lom closed at 4:30 PM, and directed me to Suan Dok Hospital instead. I came to Pai Lom because I'm a student and I didn't want to face the long queues at Suan Dok, so I used my medical benefits. Therefore, I didn't receive treatment because Pai Lom didn't announce the testing times for people at risk of COVID-19. They didn't post any information on their website. There was only an A4 sheet of paper taped to the table and the wall in front of Pai Lom.

Chiang Mai University Health Center (Phai Lom): For first-time visitors, we recommend parking across from Female Dormitory 1. There are restaurants, an optician, and a pharmacy nearby, offering complete facilities.

I went to the hospital two days in a row for respiratory checkups. It was a different doctor each time, but their personalities and egos were the same. Perhaps it's because they're older; everything they said seemed abrupt and irritating. They seemed especially annoyed when they found out what was wrong with me (the patient). If they were annoyed, they should have at least examined me more thoroughly! They rushed the examination so much, I don't know where they were rushing to. We talked for less than three minutes each, like playing a question-and-answer game. I recommend anyone planning to go there or who is sick to do a lot of research beforehand, because if you don't know and can't answer the questions, you won't know what the results will be. I was quite confused, because if you need to know what you're sick with, why go to the doctor? I had a fever for several days, a high fever, but I was taking fever reducers. How could I have a fever during the examination? 🥹 They didn't ask any detailed questions, just rushed through the discussion, like they were judging me and concluding what was wrong instead of being sure. They told me I had a sore throat when I had been bedridden for three days with a high fever every night. In the end, I had to do my own research and tell them what was wrong, and then get a medical certificate. It's like their only job is to sit there and issue medical certificates. If anyone received good service, congratulations, because I won't be going back again. Exhausted from fever and medication, I still had to answer questions correctly and quickly. The queue was long, but the queue management was terrible. It felt like there weren't that many people on the day I went; they should have organized the system better and more consistently, not kept changing it. I felt sorry for the nurses walking around the building looking for people. The diagnosis was also wrong. I understand people make mistakes, but it was quite upsetting. The way they worked felt like they weren't putting in their full effort. The doctors didn't seem to see me as an ordinary patient, but more like medical students who needed to know medical knowledge. Luckily, I'm also a health science student, but I wouldn't do what the doctors did if I were a patient. Please improve this. I usually trust all doctors, but after this, I'm done. I can't trust anyone but myself. I don't know the internal system, but being a doctor or nurse is your job. You should have more empathy for students or see them as human beings. You shouldn't expect patients to know everything or do everything instantly. If you've been sick yourself, you'll understand.

I came to get my flu and dengue fever vaccinations (on a Saturday).
The place is clean, well-organized, and the management is systematic and efficient. The staff are polite and provide excellent service. The entire process took only half an hour.

I used my universal healthcare card at Suan Dok Hospital. I arrived at 8:40, got a queue number, had my blood pressure checked, and filled out the forms by 8:47. I saw the doctor immediately; he was a retired professor. The examination finished at 9:00, and then I waited another ten minutes. A nurse came and informed me that they had scheduled my next appointment and I could go pick up my medication now. It was very quick.
Students from Chiang Mai University receive free treatment here, so I've been coming here every day to get my wounds bandaged since my bike accident. …

It's nice, clean and modern. But the finance department takes too long for lunch, starting work late in the afternoon. People waiting to pay are left waiting, confused, like... "What are we waiting for?" They're nudging each other, wondering what's going on. Other departments seem to have nurses rotating shifts during lunchtime, so I wonder if the finance department doesn't have rotating shifts for lunch?

The quality of service is considered good, acceptable.
Students or university staff can claim reimbursement. I don't know about other departments.
Some doctors and nurses have very high egos, I don't know why. Overall, it's acceptable.

The service is fast, the place is clean, and there's parking available. It's convenient for students and staff of Chiang Mai University.

If possible, I would like to suggest that some of the service staff use standard Thai for communication. Because not all of the customers are from Northern Thailand, they may not understand immediately what to do, which could lead to delays or mistakes, and frustrate the staff.
Good service, not many customers.

The staff, doctors, and nurses were okay and provided good service, but the finance staff were terrible. They spoke rudely and without politeness, didn't inform me when I was finished, and even had the nerve to ask what I was waiting for.

I called to book an appointment for my flu shot and came as scheduled. The queuing system was fast and efficient. The air conditioning was nice and cool, and the staff giving the shot were friendly and made me feel relaxed.
I went to the dentist. The dentist was nice and polite, but the assistant was very rude and aggressive. And I wasn't asking for free treatment, so I changed clinics immediately.
I've been here for my second vaccination. The service was good and fast. I appreciate their focus on safe sex for students, and they give out free condoms and HIV test kits.

I don't understand the queuing system; they didn't inform me of anything, just told me to sit and wait. When I went to ask, they spoke in a rude tone, even though I asked politely. I've been sitting and waiting for almost two hours and …
No one answered the phone.
Terrible service. I waited 5 hours to get my wound treated. A complete waste of my time.
I had a check-up with a dermatologist today. It was quick, only 3 minutes, and I was able to get medication, but the cause of my condition is still unknown.
I've been there twice, and the nurses were very polite, and the doctor was good too.
I've been waiting for so long, I don't know where the doctor went. I've been here since 3 PM, and it
The finance staff were very rude and acted like I was asking for something for free.

Fast service, polite staff.

It's extremely hot. Being sick is already painful. The seating arrangements should be better. I understand the need to separate people with respiratory illnesses from others, but the space should be appropriate for Thailand's hot climate. The nurses seemed attentive, but it didn't make me feel any more comfortable. I was so hot I felt like I was going to faint.
